sample-eosb-guide/2.title: End of Service Benefit Guide (sample)
sample-eosb-guide/2.text:
Introduction

This sample guide explains how an end of service benefit is worked out for workers in the private sector. It is synthetic text written to test the Dalil reviewer screen and is not an official publication.

Who this guide is for

Workers on full-time contracts, their employers, and anyone helping a worker check a final settlement.

sample-eosb-guide/4.title: End of Service Benefit Guide (sample)
sample-eosb-guide/4.text:
Section 3. Calculating the end of service benefit

3.1 A worker employed under a full-time contract who has completed at least one year of continuous service is entitled to an end of service benefit when the contract ends.

3.2 The benefit is calculated on the basic wage most recently paid, excluding allowances for housing, transport and other items.

3.3 For the first five years of service, the benefit equals 21 days of basic wage for each year of service. For each year beyond five, the benefit equals 30 days of basic wage.

3.4 The total benefit may not exceed the equivalent of two years of the worker's basic wage.

3.5 Periods of unpaid absence are not counted as service when calculating the benefit.

ملخص (نص تجريبي): يستحق العامل الذي أكمل سنة واحدة على الأقل من الخدمة المتواصلة مكافأة نهاية الخدمة عند انتهاء العقد، وتحسب على أساس الأجر الأساسي.

sample-labour-regulation/12.title: Labour Relations Regulation, consolidated text (sample)
sample-labour-regulation/12.text:
Article 51. Final settlement

The employer shall pay the worker all wages and benefits due within fourteen days of the end of the contract. A worker may file a complaint with the ministry if the settlement is not paid on time.

Article 52. Work permits

Working without a valid work permit exposes both the worker and the employer to administrative fines. A worker whose permit has been cancelled may remain in the country during the grace period set out in the residence rules in order to find new work or leave.
